english.title: Conspiracy to cause public nuisance
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..) conspired with

(A)_[another, namely **(..SPECIFY OTHER PERSON..),]_
(B)_[others]_

to cause a public nuisance in that **(..SPECIFY NUISANCE ALLEGED..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) of the Criminal Law Act 1977.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
conspired with another/others to cause a public nuisance

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The common law offence is replaced by a statutory offence of intentionally or recklessly causing public nuisance under section 78 of the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022. This offence no longer applies from the 27th June 2022. For the offence applying after this date, see H100676.
(ii) This offence still applies where the act or omission began before the 17th June 2022 and continued after the new offence under section 78 of the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022 came in force.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum life mprisonment.

Time limit on Prosecutions:
None

Note
The maximum penalty on summary conviction was increased from 2nd May 2022, see section 32(1) of the Magistrates’ Courts Act 1980 as amended by section 282(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003. This applies only to offences committed on or after that date, see section 282(4). For offences committed before 2nd May 2022 the maximum penalty on summary conviction is six months imprisonment and/or a fine.
